messages:
tess: heads-up — we're getting reports from a few enterprise customers (shared-gpu tier) about sudden quota burn spikes and invoice-preview showing tokens attributed to `unknown_route`. looks correlated with ingress header normalization change rolled yesterday. anyone following edge header work? :grimacing:

omar: I saw the ingress change. we normalized and downcased incoming headers to enforce cache keys. nginx was configured to strip headers with commas/quotes. if a client sent `X-Route-Hint: service=foo,priority=2` nginx may have dropped it.

chet: quick repro: observed meter events in staging where `x-route-hint` missing but `x-original-path` present. suspected header cleaning in `edge-rewrite` stage. config diff from last deploy: 
```nginx
# OLD: preserve all headers
proxy_set_header X-Route-Hint $http_x_route_hint;
# NEW: sanitize commas -> can drop complex hints 
proxy_set_header X-Route-Hint $sanitized_x_route_hint;
```
This sanitized variable strips commas.

abby: if meter plane relies on `X-Route-Hint` for quota attribution we just created a class of requests that fall back to default routing => higher unit cost/incorrect invoice attribution. we need a short mitigation flow: 1) stop dropping the header, 2) emit a conservative fallback tag so we can trace affected events, 3) plan a backfill.

tess: Agreed. quick mitigation options: A) revert sanitize change (risky at scale), B) add a new header `X-Route-Hint-B64` where edge base64-encodes original hint (safe), C) have router merge query param `?route_hint=` into metadata (breaks caching). I favor B for minimal blast radius.

omar: B is clean. encode and set `X-Route-Hint-B64` in ingress before downstream caches. small patch on ingress lua: 
```lua
local hint = ngx.req.get_headers()["x-route-hint"]
if hint then ngx.req.set_header("x-route-hint-b64", ngx.encode_base64(hint)) end
```
Feature-flag it for 0.1% traffic first.

chet: I'll open the hotfix PR with the lua snippet and a unit test for the header preservation. also adding telemetry: increment `billing.header.missing_x_route_hint` when meter events arrive without either header. create an alert if >50 in 10m.

billing-bot: ALERT: billing.header.missing_x_route_hint = 127 (10m) — paging billing-oncall.

abby: good. for verification we'll produce a small dashboard card comparing token share grouped by `route_hint` vs `route_hint_b64` presence. SQL sketch for the metering warehouse: 
```sql
SELECT coalesce(route_hint, route_hint_b64) as hint_key, SUM(tokens) as tokens
FROM metering.events
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '6 hours'
GROUP BY hint_key
ORDER BY tokens DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
This will show how many tokens fell into the unknown bucket.

deploy-bot: staging deploy of hotfix/ingress-hint-preserve succeeded — build 4688 (staging).

omar: will ship FF at 0.1% in staging then 0.1% in prod tomorrow morning. once we see events with `x-route-hint-b64` land in meter pipeline we can widen.

chet: after canary we should run a backfill: scan requests for missing `route_hint` during the incident window and reconstruct hint from access logs (they still contain raw header in edge logs), then emit correction events to ledger with `correction=true`. coordinate with invoice-audit; avoid changing already-closed invoices.

abby: add runbook entry "header-normalization -> missing-route-hint" with mitigation steps: FF canary, dashboard query, alert thresholds, and backfill path. who owns runbook edit?

tess: I'll update the runbook and notify invoice-audit before any backfill. target timeline: canary today 16:00 UTC at 0.1%, monitor 2h, then increase to 5% if healthy.

omar: also adding traces: include `ingress.decision=preserve_b64|sanitize` in emitted meter metadata so we can pivot quickly.

billing-bot: NOTE: invoice-audit requested a pre-backfill diff report and stakeholder signoff.

abby: thanks everyone. short-term: watch the alert and the dashboard. medium-term: add an integ test covering header preservation across ingress -> edge cache -> meter pipeline so this doesn't regress. :thumbsup:
